correctness.rationale: The proof reduces five erasures to largest eigenvalue of the deleted 5x5 Gram. Exact pairwise Gauss magnitudes and triangle holonomies characterize every equality mask as five distinct slopes on one affine line with all positive Paley triple signs. A direct exact enumeration excludes all 7476 five-sets at p=5,13,17; nine certified positive witnesses cover p=29..101. For p>=109, Paley triangles exist, the exact common-nonneighbor count (p-3-tau)/8 and Hasse |tau|<=2sqrt(p) exceed Hoffman alpha(P_p)<=sqrt(p), giving an induced K3 disjoint union K2. No finite testing is used as proof for unbounded primes. The checker at CHECK.py was executed and passed.

originality.rationale: The five-erasure prime-29 onset and all-prime existence proof are not supplied by the inspected general ETF switching criterion, Alltop three-erasure result or four-column Paley spectral census. Specifically the four-column real Paley result computes four-subset signs but does not decide coherent five-subset existence at primes 13,17,29 or prove it thereafter. The new proof uses a five-vertex induced-graph condition, Hasse plus Hoffman and exact nine-prime witnesses. Residual classical Paley switching-priority risk is documented.
residual_risks: An older result on induced K3 disjoint union K2 in prime Paley graphs, or switching-clique numbers of symmetric conference frames, may already imply the sharp 29 threshold under different terminology.

value.rationale: The existence/attainment transition for five exact adversarial measurement losses is a naturally defined sharp stability boundary of a canonical deterministic overcomplete Gabor frame. It is nontrivial after four-column coherence is known: p13 and p17 admit four-way phase alignment but forbid five, while every admissible prime p>=29 permits five. The proof connects the frame optimum to a five-vertex Paley induced pattern and a cubic elliptic character sum; this identifies a usable exact dimension threshold and the full geometry of attaining masks. It does not claim a global five-erasure optimum in nonattaining residue classes.
